justification: counsel: Option C is the strongest distractor only by borrowing the passage's statement that measurements barely moved across fourteen summers and applying that stability to the villages in the prompt. | dies: The passage expressly limits that stability to places where the frame was stored: "Där stommen – stången med sina tvärslåar och järnringar – togs in och sparades till nästa sommar rörde sig måtten knappt över de fjorton somrarna." For villages that did not save it, the text instead says that proportions drifted and "tycks ha närmat sig formen i den närmaste by som hade en sparad stomme att gå efter", which directly supports B. A reverses that direction, and D confuses a later preservation request with what determined the form. All three distractors are cleanly wrong.

counsel: Option B can be made superficially attractive by treating the stored frame, with its pre-bored holes, as an external reminder of the prior structural design when the pole was assembled again. | dies: That reading does not survive the option's full wording or the repaired paragraph boundary. The text says the builder "behöver varken minnas eller besluta något", not that the frame merely supports memory, and then narrows its function: "Stommen för bara skelettet vidare." The Rossmåla example shows that leaf decoration changed even though the frame was saved, so the frame was not a memory aid for how the pole should be "lövas på nytt". D alone matches both halves: structural form persists while decoration can be redesigned. A contradicts "Vi har aldrig bestämt hur den ska se ut", and C invents an origin claim the passage never makes. All three distractors are cleanly wrong.
